title: Amending an Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI) notification
text:
If you made a mistake in your notification

 You may need to amend an Enterprise Management Incentives ( EMI ) notification if you made a mistake when you originally notified HMRC.

 What you need to do depends on when:

 • the option was granted

 • you find the mistake

 You do not need to submit a corrected notification for a minor mistake, such as a spelling error. Keep a record of the employees affected and the date the EMI options were granted in case HMRC needs this during a compliance check.

 To make an amendment, you must tell HMRC by the notification deadline.

 The deadline is:

 • 92 days after the option was granted, if it was granted on or before 5 April 2024

 • 6 July following the end of the tax year in which the option was granted, if it was granted on or after 6 April 2024

 If you are within the notification deadline

 You can submit a new notification with the correct information if you find the mistake before the deadline.

 You should report the original incorrect option as cancelled when you submit your next EMI annual return.

 If the notification deadline has passed

 If it is within 9 months since you notified HMRC

 You should contact HMRC with a reasonable excuse for why you need to amend the notification.

 If HMRC accepts your reasonable excuse, they’ll give you a code. You can use this code to submit the corrected notification through the Employment Related Securities ( ERS ) online service.

 You should report the original incorrect option as cancelled when you submit your next EMI annual return.

 If it is more than 9 months since you notified HMRC

 You cannot correct the notification if it is more than 9 months since you originally notified HMRC about the option.

 You should still tell HMRC about the mistake. They’ll consider whether:

 • the mistake was material

 • the option meets the legislative requirements for tax-advantaged treatment

 How to tell HMRC

 When you contact HMRC about a mistake, include:

 • details of the original EMI notification

 • the company name

 • the scheme name

 • the unique scheme reference number

 • details of the mistake, when you found it and why you need to correct it

 You’ll also need to give details of your reasonable excuse if the deadline has passed but it is within 9 months of the date you originally notified HMRC about the option.

 Send the information by email to shareschemes@hmrc.gov.uk or write to:

Charities, Savings & International 1
HM Revenue & Customs
BX9 1AU
